NOTICE.TITLE: Regulation (EU) 2023/956 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 May 2023 on transaction monitoring obligations for payment service providers — ORIGINAL VERSION
NOTICE.CONTENTS:
Article 1 - Subject matter. This Regulation lays down obligations for payment service providers regarding the monitoring of payment transactions to detect and prevent money laundering, terrorist financing, and fraud.
Article 2 - Transaction monitoring thresholds. 1. Payment service providers shall monitor all payment transactions. 2. Transactions exceeding EUR 10,000 in a single operation shall be subject to enhanced monitoring procedures as described in Article 4. 3. Aggregate transactions from the same customer exceeding EUR 25,000 in a calendar month shall trigger a mandatory review.
Article 3 - Monitoring systems. 1. Payment service providers shall maintain automated monitoring systems capable of detecting: (a) structuring patterns indicative of smurfing; (b) rapid movement of funds through multiple accounts; (c) transactions inconsistent with the customer's established profile. 2. Monitoring rules and thresholds shall be reviewed annually and updated where necessary.
Article 4 - Enhanced monitoring procedures. For transactions subject to enhanced monitoring under Article 2, payment service providers shall conduct a manual review within 48 hours and file a SAR if suspicion is confirmed.
Article 5 - Record retention. Transaction monitoring records shall be retained for five years.
Article 6 - Entry into force. This Regulation enters into force on 1 November 2023.
